description: SoCal Robotics & STEM Foundation is a nonprofit supporting robotics teams and STEM education across Southern California. We provide mentorship, tools, and competition support to students who want to design, build, and program real machines — no prior experience required.
meetingTime: Saturdays, 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM at the Innovation Lab
moreText: Want to get involved? Students, mentors, and sponsors are all welcome — come to a Saturday session or reach out below.

events.title: Fall Build Season Kickoff
events.description: First Saturday session of the season — meet your team and get hands-on with this year's kit of parts.

events.title: Regional Qualifier
events.description: Our teams compete for a spot at the state championship.

awards.title: Regional Innovation Award
awards.description: Recognized for our student-designed outreach curriculum.

heroLead: SoCal Robotics & STEM Foundation is a nonprofit supporting robotics teams and STEM education across Southern California. We provide mentorship, tools, and competition support to students who want to design, build, and program real machines — no prior experience required.

process.title: Mentor & teach
process.description: We coach rookie FTC and FLL teams, run workshops, and bring robotics into classrooms across Southern California — because someone did the same for us.

process.title: Design & build
process.description: Every arm, drivetrain and mechanism is engineered, machined and iterated by students — from CAD to competition day.

process.title: Code & strategize
process.description: Our programmers write autonomous routines and drive software from scratch, then scout and strategize alliance by alliance.

testimonial.quote: Robotics didn't just teach me to code — it taught me to lead.
testimonial.attribution: A student officer, SoCal Robotics & STEM Foundation

homeAboutText: SoCal Robotics & STEM Foundation is led by advisor Dr. Elena Marsh and a student officer team, meeting Saturdays, 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM at the Innovation Lab. We support robotics teams and STEM education across Southern California with mentorship, tools, and competition support for students who want to design, build, and program real machines.
